descriptor.assumptions: Mole fractions are used as proxies for ionic charge: alkali ions counted as +1 and divalent alkaline-earth/Mg as +2, ignoring that only a fraction may be hydroxide-bound or ionized. osda_charge is taken as the formal charge magnitude of a single OSDA molecule scaled by its gel mole fraction; neutral OSDAs or sda1 = 0 give a large ratio by construction (dominated by the 0.002 safeguard), which is intentional since inorganic cations then dominate charge balance. The ratio says nothing about OH-, F- mineralizers or Ge/B heteroatom chemistry, which can override this balance.
descriptor.expected_effect: As the ratio increases (inorganic cations dominating), likelihood of inorganic-directed phases such as LTA, FAU, CHA, LEV and dense/Failed outcomes should rise, while OSDA-templated high-silica phases such as MFI, MTW, *BEA and MWW should become less likely. Very large values (effectively no charged OSDA) should correspond to OSDA-free alkali-aluminosilicate syntheses. Low values should shift predictions toward OSDA-templated frameworks.
descriptor.falsification: If the descriptor carries no synthesis-relevant information, held-out publication accuracy will not change when it is added, or feature importance will be near zero. It is also falsified if phases like MTW or *BEA appear across the full range of the ratio with no systematic separation from LTA/FAU/CHA, since then cation/OSDA charge balance is not a discriminating axis.
descriptor.hypothesis: The competition between inorganic cations and the OSDA for charge-balancing roles in the gel steers phase selectivity: recipes where the inorganic cationic charge dominates over the organic cationic charge should favor inorganic-templated, low-silica or small-pore frameworks, whereas recipes where the OSDA charge dominates should favor OSDA-templated high-silica frameworks.
descriptor.mechanism: Framework T-atom substitution (Al, B, Ga, divalent heteroatoms) creates framework charge that must be balanced by cations; OSDA charge density matching and cation-OSDA-defect charge ordering determine which framework topology can crystallize. When inorganic charge far exceeds OSDA charge, the OSDA cannot act as the primary template and Na/K-rich regimes direct dense or small-pore phases (LTA, FAU, CHA, sodalite-like, P1) or amorphous products; when OSDA charge dominates, the OSDA fills the pores and high-silica large-pore phases (MFI, MTW, *BEA, MWW) are stabilized. The literature repeatedly shows that phase selectivity with a fixed OSDA flips depending on the inorganic cation content (Na/Rb choline EU-12; Na synergy with Et6-diquat-5 giving P1 vs SUZ-4 vs MOR; charge density mismatch between organic and inorganic SDAs), so a single scalar capturing this balance should transfer across unseen publications. Because trees split on one column, this ratio makes an emergent balance directly available.
descriptor.name: inorganic_to_osda_charge_ratio

descriptor.assumptions: The formula assumes fluoride and OSDA/trivalent-species mole fractions in the normalized gel are a faithful proxy for the actual HF/OSDA and Si/Al ratios in the published recipes, which is only approximately true because normalization by total moles (including large water fractions) compresses these ratios differently across papers. It assumes Al, B and Ga play a similar charge-compensating role, ignoring that B is more easily rejected by the framework and that P (in aluminophosphate syntheses) and divalent heteroatoms (Zn, Mg) follow different charge rules; these syntheses will show descriptor values driven only by their F and sda1 content. F-source identity (NH4F vs HF) and OH content, which also matter, are not captured by this descriptor alone.
descriptor.expected_effect: As the descriptor increases from 0: fluoride-free hydroxide-type aluminosilicate phases (FAU, LTA, MOR, low-silica CHA) should give way to fluoride-route high-silica phases; at moderate values (~1) D4R-containing high-silica phases such as *BEA/BEC, MTW, UTL and pure-silica MFI become accessible; at very high values (>1.5) small-pore or excess-fluoride-specific phases (AEL, AEI, LEV-type high-silica products) or Failed (over-mineralized, slow-crystallizing gels) become more likely. Very low values with high Al should also raise Failed probability (dense/amorphous phases from fast hydroxide crystallization).
descriptor.falsification: If the descriptor carries no phase-selective information, the distributions of F/(sda1+Al+B+Ga) should be statistically indistinguishable across the product classes (e.g., *BEA vs MFI vs FER vs Failed) on held-out publications, or the direction of the effect should reverse: fluoride-rich recipes should not systematically differ in outcome from fluoride-poor recipes at fixed OSDA/Al chemistry. Also falsified if fluoride-free gels (descriptor = 0) show the same phase distribution as high-fluoride gels with the same OSDA and Si/Al.
descriptor.hypothesis: The ratio of fluoride in the gel to the total charge-directing species available to pair with it (OSDA cations plus trivalent framework heteroatoms Al, B, Ga) controls whether the synthesis proceeds along a fluoride-mineralized, defect-free high-silica pathway or an Al-charge-balanced pathway, and thus which framework crystallizes. Recipes with fluoride in excess of the available OSDA and trivalent centers (high value of this descriptor) should favor phases known from excess-fluoride synthesis (e.g., small-pore or novel high-silica phases such as *BEA at HF/OSDA = 1, FER/RUT mixtures at low HF/OSDA shifting to ERS-7-like phases at HF/OSDA ~ 2), while recipes where Al greatly exceeds fluoride (low value) should favor aluminosilicate phases crystallized in hydroxide media (LTA, FAU, MOR, CHA, TON), and zero-fluoride recipes collapse to the hydroxide-route limit.
descriptor.mechanism: Fluoride acts both as a mineralizer and as an occluded anion: in near-neutral fluoride media it can sit inside small cages of the framework (e.g., D4R units in *BEA, UTL, LTA-type germanosilicates) or pair with divalent/trivalent heteroatoms, compensating framework charge instead of creating silanol defects. When F- is scarce relative to OSDA+ (Al+B+Ga), the OSDA cations must be balanced by [AlO4/2]- or [BO4/2]- framework charges, which stabilizes heteroatom-containing frameworks and suppresses pure-silica phases (e.g., pure-silica beta remains amorphous at HF/OSDA <= 0.5, but forms at HF/OSDA = 1.0; pure-silica ZSM-5 appears at intermediate HF/OSDA). When F- is in large excess, heteroatom incorporation and F- cage occlusion compete, and phase selectivity shifts entirely (FER/RUT at HF/Ch+ <= 1 becomes ERS-7 at HF/Ch+ = 2; excess fluoride enables PST-21/22-type new phases). A tree ensemble can split directly on this single ratio, which is not expressible from the individual mole fractions alone.

descriptor.assumptions: Assumes crystallization is approximately isothermal during the recorded cryst_time and that an Arrhenius-type product T*log(t) with T in Celsius is a serviceable proxy for the true time-temperature exposure integral (no activation energy is fitted; the Celsius offset is not physically exact but preserves ordering at fixed t). log10 compresses the wide range of crystallization times so that long runs do not dominate. This is a kinetic-severity proxy only: it ignores heating/cooling ramps, seeding, and gel composition effects already captured elsewhere.
descriptor.expected_effect: As thermal_dose increases, 'Failed' outcomes should first decrease (gels cross the nucleation threshold) and then rise or shift toward dense/thermodynamically stable products at very high dose; metastable, low-temperature frameworks (FAU, LTA, layered MWW) should concentrate at intermediate dose, while refractory high-silica phases tolerate higher dose before transforming.
descriptor.falsification: If the product-phase distribution is essentially invariant when thermal_dose is varied while holding cryst_temp and cryst_time fixed within their observed ranges (i.e., the model gains no split quality from thermal_dose beyond the existing time and temperature columns), or if Failed and phase-transformed outcomes occur uniformly across the thermal_dose range, the hypothesis is contradicted.
descriptor.hypothesis: The product of crystallization temperature and the logarithm of crystallization time (an Arrhenius-inspired 'thermal dose') governs whether a gel reaches nucleation, fully crystallizes, or over-crystallizes into a secondary/dense phase. Recipes with low thermal dose should end in 'Failed' (insufficient nucleation/growth), intermediate dose should yield the metastable OSDA-templated target phase, and high dose should favor thermodynamically more stable or denser phases (e.g., transformation of FAU to denser phases, loss of layered MWW-type precursors to condensed products) or impurity mixtures.
descriptor.mechanism: Zeolite crystallization kinetics are thermally activated; the extent of reaction scales roughly with an integral of temperature-weighted time (analogous to an Arrhenius exposure). Nucleation requires a minimum thermal dose; once crystals form, continued hydrothermal exposure drives Ostwald ripening and solution-mediated phase transformation, because metastable zeolites dissolve when not in equilibrium with the mother liquor. Tree ensembles receive cryst_temp and cryst_time as separate columns and can only split on one at a time, so this exposure-like combination is not directly available to the model.
